title: The BIGGEST Wealth Transfer of the Next Decade Starts HERE
speaker: Ross Givens

macro_themes.view: AI runs on electricity and the US stopped building power for 20 years, so money over the next 10 years flows to power generation, grid gear and fuel.
Last decade's winners may be priced like Cisco in 2000; great businesses at the wrong price.

calls.reason: Gas-turbine bottleneck with $176B backlog and turbine agreements into 2031; not cheap but demand for power persists. Long-term thesis: the next decade rewards hard-to-replace AI power infrastructure (generation, grid equipment, nuclear fuel) rather than cheap-to-scale software.
calls.quote: GE Vernova, Eaton, and Cameco are the three names I'd want on my side for the next 10 years

calls.reason: Sells switchgear/transformers; 307 GW US data-center backlog (15 years of work) plus reshoring factories give two demand engines and a cushion if AI spending pauses.
calls.quote: Eaton gets paid when AI builds, and it gets paid when manufacturing comes home

calls.reason: Long-term uranium contract price at a record $96.50/lb while stock sits in mid-80s, a year-long buy zone, over a third below its 135 52-week high.
calls.quote: I would much rather buy when a product is at a record and the stock is on sale

notes: CCJ price 'mid-80s' recorded as 85. Medium-term CCJ bias inferred from 'buy zone' framing; he says he can't promise the gap closes next month.
